metadata.description: Web app name. The portal address is https://<appName>.azurewebsites.net. Must be globally unique.
Region of your virtual network. The web app, PostgreSQL, Key Vault and the private endpoints are created in this region.
App Service plan size. See docs/SIZING.md.

Zone redundancy of the App Service plan: the instances run in different availability zones. Azure chooses the zones; App Service has no setting for them. Needs a Premium plan (P0v3 or larger) and a region with availability zones. The portal supports more than one instance.
Instances of the App Service plan. With zone redundancy at least 2: Azure spreads them over the availability zones of the region, so 3 instances in a region with three zones run one in each zone.

Code: the workflow deploy-appservice.yml uploads the built app to the built-in .NET 10 runtime. Container: the web app runs the image from Azure Container Registry; the workflow deploy-appservice-container.yml builds and pushes it.
Microsoft Entra tenant id of the app registration.
Application (client) id of the app registration (setup-sp.ps1 prints it).
Client secret of the app registration.

Resource id of an existing subnet for the VNet integration of the web app: /subscriptions/<id>/resourceGroups/<group>/providers/Microsoft.Network/virtualNetworks/<vnet>/subnets/<subnet>. Only for App Service and delegated to Microsoft.Web/serverFarms (the deployment does not change your subnets). /28 or larger, /26 recommended.

Resource id of an existing subnet for the private endpoints of the web app, PostgreSQL, Key Vault and the container registry. The four parameters below put single private endpoints into other subnets.
Optional: subnet for the private endpoint of the web app. Empty = privateEndpointSubnetResourceId. The subnet of an existing private endpoint cannot be changed: delete the endpoint first.
AzurePostgreSQL only, optional: subnet for the private endpoint of PostgreSQL. Empty = privateEndpointSubnetResourceId.
Optional: subnet for the private endpoint of the Key Vault (new vault, or existing vault with existingKeyVaultPrivateEndpoint). Empty = privateEndpointSubnetResourceId.
Container only, optional: subnet for the private endpoint of the registry (new registry, or existing registry with existingContainerRegistryPrivateEndpoint). Empty = privateEndpointSubnetResourceId.
Existing private DNS zone privatelink.azurewebsites.net, for example in a hub subscription. Empty = create one in this resource group and link it to the VNet of the app subnet.
AzurePostgreSQL only: existing private DNS zone privatelink.postgres.database.azure.com. Empty = create one in this resource group and link it to the VNet of the app subnet.

Existing private DNS zone privatelink.vaultcore.azure.net. Empty = create one in this resource group and link it to the VNet of the app subnet. Not needed for an existing vault without a new private endpoint.

Container: existing private DNS zone privatelink.azurecr.io. Empty = create one in this resource group and link it to the VNet of the app subnet. Not needed for an existing registry without a new private endpoint.
AzurePostgreSQL: the template creates Azure Database for PostgreSQL Flexible Server. ExistingServer: your own PostgreSQL server, for example on a VM; the template creates no database server.
AzurePostgreSQL only. ManagedIdentity: the portal signs in with its managed identity (Microsoft Entra), no password. Password: administrator login and password.
ExistingServer only: connection string with login and password, for example Host=pg01.contoso.com;Port=5432;Database=accessreview;Username=accessreview;Password=<password>;Ssl Mode=VerifyFull
ExistingServer only, optional: CA certificate of the server (base64 of the .cer file, or PEM) when the server certificate comes from your own CA. Needed for Ssl Mode=VerifyFull.
AzurePostgreSQL only: server name (globally unique, lower case). Empty = psql-<appName>.
AzurePostgreSQL with Password only: administrator password of the server. Do not use ; or quotes.

PostgreSQL compute size. The tier follows from the name: Standard_B = Burstable, Standard_D = General Purpose, Standard_E = Memory Optimized. Burstable sizes are not available for every subscription in every region (SkuNotAvailable). See docs/SIZING.md.
PostgreSQL storage in GB (32, 64, 128, 256, 512, ...). Storage auto-grow is on.
High availability of PostgreSQL: ZoneRedundant = standby server in another availability zone, SameZone = standby in the same zone. Not with Burstable sizes. The standby doubles the compute cost.
Availability zone of the PostgreSQL server: 1, 2 or 3. Empty = Azure chooses. Used only when Azure creates the server: a later deployment with another zone does not move the server.
With postgresHighAvailability = ZoneRedundant: availability zone of the standby server, 1, 2 or 3, another zone than postgresAvailabilityZone. Empty = Azure chooses.
Key Vault name (3-24 characters, globally unique). Empty = a name derived from the resource group and the app name.
Resource group of the Key Vault, in the same subscription. It must exist. Empty = the resource group of the deployment. The Key Vault always has a private endpoint and no public access.
Purge protection of the Key Vault. With it, a deleted vault name stays reserved until the retention period ends.

Resource id of an existing Key Vault that uses Azure RBAC (permission model "Azure role-based access control"), in any subscription of the tenant. The template adds the secrets <appName>-client-secret and <appName>-db-connection and gives id-<appName> the role Key Vault Secrets User. It changes nothing else in the vault. Empty = the template creates a new vault (keyVaultName, keyVaultResourceGroup, enablePurgeProtection).
Existing Key Vault: scope of the role Key Vault Secrets User for id-<appName>. Secrets = only the two secrets of the portal (for a vault that other apps also use). Vault = all secrets of the vault.

Existing Key Vault: create a private endpoint for the vault in the private endpoint subnet, with its record in the zone privatelink.vaultcore.azure.net. false = the vault already has a private endpoint that the App Service subnet reaches, for example in a hub network with central DNS zones.

Container: resource id of an existing Azure Container Registry, in any subscription of the tenant. id-<appName> gets the pull role: AcrPull, or Container Registry Repository Reader for a registry with ABAC repository permissions. Empty = the template creates a new registry (Premium, private endpoint, no public access, no admin user).

Container with an existing registry: create a private endpoint for the registry in the private endpoint subnet, with its records in the zone privatelink.azurecr.io. false = the registry already has a private endpoint that the App Service subnet reaches.
Container with a new registry: registry name (5-50 letters and digits, globally unique). Empty = cr<unique string>.
Container: repository and tag of the portal image in the registry. The workflow deploy-appservice-container.yml pushes the tags <commit> and latest, and switches the web app to <commit>.

metadata.description: Server name (globally unique, lower case).
PostgreSQL major version.
Administrator login. Only with passwordAuth = true.
Administrator password. Only with passwordAuth = true.
Sign-in with administratorLogin and administratorPassword. false = Microsoft Entra authentication only.
Microsoft Entra administrators of the server: objects { objectId, principalName, principalType (User, Group or ServicePrincipal) }.
Compute size. Standard_D2ds_v5 (2 vCores, 8 GB) is enough for tens of thousands of assignments per scan; use D4ds_v5 for very large tenants.
Storage in GB. Each snapshot row needs about 2-3 KB including indexes.
Availability zone of the server (1, 2 or 3). Empty = Azure chooses. Used only when Azure creates the server: a later deployment with another zone does not move it.
With highAvailability = ZoneRedundant: availability zone of the standby server, another zone than availabilityZone. Empty = Azure chooses.
Database used by the portal.
Public access: client IP ranges allowed to connect (for example the pipeline agent and the portal host).
Public access: allow connections from Azure services (App Service, Container Apps without VNet integration).
Without a delegated subnet: false = no public endpoint and no firewall rules, for a server that you reach through a private endpoint.
Private access: resource id of a subnet delegated to Microsoft.DBforPostgreSQL/flexibleServers. Empty = public access.
Private access: resource id of the private DNS zone (privatelink.postgres.database.azure.com or <name>.private.postgres.database.azure.com).
Also allow Microsoft Entra ID authentication (for administrators and managed identities).
